title: Overnight Smoked Brisket Hold
seoTitle: Overnight Smoked Brisket Hold | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Start at midnight, slice at dinner—built for hall scheduling
subtitle: Low-and-slow packer that finishes before shift and holds hot for ten
description: Adapted from classic overnight brisket hold methods (Traeger, Hey Grill Hey): a trimmed packer rides 225°F through the night, wraps in the stall, finishes probe-tender, and rests in a cooler until the crew rolls in.

steps.title: Prep and season
steps.instruction: Trim fat cap to 1/4 inch. Coat with mustard, then salt, pepper, and onion powder. Rest 30 minutes while smoker preheats to 225°F.

steps.title: Overnight smoke
steps.instruction: Place brisket fat-side up at 225°F. Smoke undisturbed until internal temp reaches 160–165°F and bark is set, about 7–8 hours.

steps.title: Wrap for the finish
steps.instruction: Wrap in butcher paper with a splash of broth. Continue at 225°F until flat probes 203°F and feels like soft butter, about 3–4 hours.

steps.title: Cooler rest
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped brisket in an insulated cooler at least 90 minutes—this is where the magic happens for slice-ready meat.

steps.title: Slice for service
steps.instruction: Unwrap, slice flat against the grain 1/4 inch thick. Toss lightly with warm broth. Reserve point for burnt ends or chop for sandwiches.

steps.title: 170°F warm hold
steps.instruction: Transfer sliced brisket to a hotel pan, add 1/2 cup broth, cover tightly with foil, and hold at 170°F until the line opens.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: Brisket tray with broth for moistening, pickles, and toast. Call it: overnight brisket—slice and stack.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Vacuum or wrap tight; reheat slices in hot broth at 325°F covered until 165°F internal.

proTips: Use a leave-in probe alarm so you don't have to wake up to check temps.
Cooler rest is not optional—it's how you hit a 6 AM finish with noon service.
If brisket finishes early, keep it whole wrapped in the cooler; slice on demand.
tonightSpread: Sliced brisket in a hotel pan with broth.
Pickles, onion, and Texas toast for sandwiches.
leftovers: Brisket breakfast burritos with eggs and salsa.
Chop into chili for the next cold shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The cook happens while the hall sleeps. By dinner you have rested, slice-ready brisket without babysitting the pit between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Plan 12–14 hours total. Hold whole wrapped brisket in a cooler up to 6 hours. For extended hold, slice and pan with broth at 170°F—never above 175°F or lean meat dries.
